❖ blood transfusion is not recommended unless:\n◇ The Hb concentration is <7 g/dL\n◇ The patient requires increased oxygen-carrying capacity (cardiopulmonary disease).
Normally, this point is reached between 8 and 12 wk of age, when the Hb concentration is about 11 g/dL.

Haemoglobin
The haemoglobin (Hb) concentration in blood from the
umbilical cord is high with a mean of 17 g/dl (17 g/100 ml).
Values up to 20 g/dl may be recorded.

snip.t: The Hb concentration continues to decline until tissue oxygen needs become greater than oxygen delivery.\n
MCHC — mean cell Hb concentration (Hb relative to cell volume)
